title: Shift 2D Grid
summary: For a grid of dimensions m x n, perform k shift operations.
statement: For a grid of dimensions m x n, perform k shift operations. Each shift moves each element to the right by one column, wrapping around to the first column at the end of a row. The last element of each row wraps to the first column of the next row, and the last element of the last row wraps to the first column of the first row. After k shifts, return the modified grid.
constraints: Shift every cell right k times with row wrapping.
reference_solution:
def shift_grid(grid, k):
 flat=sum(grid,[]);k%=len(flat)
 if k:flat=flat[-k:]+flat[:-k]
 width=len(grid[0]);return [flat[i:i+width] for i in range(0,len(flat),width)]

hints: Flatten row-major order so one right shift is a cyclic shift by one.
Reduce k modulo total cells and rotate the flat list.
Slice the rotated values back into rows of the original width.
Row-major flattening preserves exactly the required wrap order.
